paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates estimated Hessian trace values (noted in the title as “Traces × 10⁻⁵”) for the COPA setting as a function of adapter rank. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” on a linear scale with four discrete tick values at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis is unlabeled but corresponds to the trace values shown on a linear scale with labeled ticks at 0.0, 0.5, and 1.0 (spaced by 0.5), spanning roughly from 0 up to a bit above 1.0. A single series is shown as a solid black line connecting orange square markers, with black vertical error bars (with caps) at each rank. The series is near 0.30 at rank 4 (error bar approximately 0.10 to 0.50), decreases slightly to about 0.28 at rank 16 (approximately 0.20 to 0.35), increases to about 0.67 at rank 64 (approximately 0.48 to 0.85), and increases again to about 0.73 at rank 256 (approximately 0.50 to 0.98).
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates estimated Hessian trace values (shown as “Traces × 10⁻⁵ (COPA)”) as a function of adapter rank. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” and uses a linear scale with four discrete tick labels at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis is unlabeled but corresponds to the trace magnitude implied by the title; it uses a linear scale with labeled ticks at 0.0, 0.5, and 1.0, spanning approximately from 0.0 up to a bit above 1.0. A single series is shown as a solid black line connecting four points, each point drawn with an orange square marker and accompanied by a vertical black error bar. The line starts near 0.32 at rank 4 (error bar extending roughly from about 0.12 to about 0.50), dips slightly to around 0.29 at rank 16 (error bar roughly ~0.22 to ~0.35), rises to about 0.67 at rank 64 (error bar roughly ~0.49 to ~0.85), and increases slightly further to around 0.73 at rank 256 (error bar roughly ~0.49 to ~0.98).
